correctness.rationale: The three formulas hold for all positive k. The Pell companion identities reduce each window sum to (B_k C_{2n+j} ± k)/m, with the specified shift j and m=16 or 2. Subtracting the first numerator leaves B_k times companion differences. Their common divisor comes from the first two adjacent differences because the step-two recurrence has unimodular transition; parity gives gcd(16,560)=16 and gcd(96,3264)=96. At primes ≥5 the remaining gcd has exactly the part of gcd(k,B_k). At 2, C_even≡1 and C_odd≡3 mod 16, B_odd≡k mod 16, and doubling gives B_k≡3k modulo 2^(v2(k)+4) for even k. Inserting these gives even-k valuations v2(k)-1,v2(k),v2(k), and zero for odd k. At 3 the recurrence makes B_odd a unit and C_odd divisible by 3. For even k, doubling from an odd index first supplies a factor 3, and each tripling of an even index contributes at least one more via 4C_j^2-1. Thus v3(B_k)>v3(k) for even k. The only extra 3 is in the c formula at k≡3 mod 6, where H(k) is prime to 3. This also gives the asserted divisibility by k. The broken-down proof covers k=1 and the infinite range of offsets. The frozen verifier was read, not run; its nominal counter of 7,620 is not a literal count of assert executions and is irrelevant to the proof.
